lessons.title: Where strip and seal belongs and the chemistry
lessons.contentBody:
Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you can:

  • Say which floors you strip and seal and which you never strip.
  • Describe what the stripper, the neutraliser and the sealer each do.

Module 8 taught you to clean hard floors safely: inspection first, the vinegar drop test, the calcareous and siliceous rule. Strip and seal is the next service up. You remove spent floor finish and lay fresh protective coats on resilient floors. It is one of the most valuable add-ons a carpet cleaner can offer, because the customer already trusts you and much of the equipment overlaps. It also carries more chemical and slip risk than anything else in the workshop, so it is taught as a disciplined sequence and not a knack.

FloorStrip and seal?Why
Vinyl sheet or VCT (vinyl composition tile)Yes, the core caseMade for a stripped and sealed acrylic finish
LinoleumYes, with careAlkali-sensitive. Use a lino-safe stripper, never a high-pH flood
LVT (luxury vinyl tile or plank)Usually no top coatMost LVT has a factory wear layer. Clean and protect it, do not strip it
Sealed timber or laminateNoWater and alkali swell the joints. Refinishing is a joiner's trade
Marble, limestone, travertineNo, and never acidCalcareous. Stone sealing is a separate discipline
Ceramic or porcelain with groutGrout seal onlyThe tile itself is not stripped

If you are not certain a floor is resilient and finish-coated, inspect it first (Module 8) and do not strip. A stripped timber floor or an etched marble floor is a five-figure mistake. That is CARSI professional judgement, not a quoted price.

The chemistry

  • Stripper: a strong alkali, often with a solvent booster, that softens and dissolves the old finish so it can be lifted. High pH, so protective equipment matters.
  • Neutraliser or rinse: a mild acid or neutral rinse that brings the floor back to neutral so the new finish bonds. Skip it and the new sealer will not adhere and will powder off.
  • Sealer or finish: a water-based acrylic or metal-cross-linked polymer laid in thin coats that level and cure to a protective, buffable film.

Source the stripper, the neutraliser and the finish from your supplier. The current label and SDS for the specific product beat any general rule here.

lessons.title: The nine steps in order
lessons.contentBody:
Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you can:

  • Run the nine steps in the right order.
  • Say why the neutral rinse is the step that decides the job.

Every step assumes Australian site conditions: a 230 V, 10 A general power outlet, RCD-protected leads, and wet-floor signage from the first drop of stripper.

  1. Inspect and confirm the floor is resilient. Check for lifting tiles and moisture, and for old tile that may contain asbestos (see the next lesson).
  2. Protect the site. Put up wet-floor signs, cordon the area, mask the skirting and edges, lift or protect adjacent carpet, and ventilate.
  3. Dust-mop or vacuum all loose grit. Grit under a pad scratches the floor.
  4. Apply stripper to a section you can manage at the label dilution and let it dwell. Do not let it dry. Re-wet if it flashes off.
  5. Agitate with a rotary machine and a stripping pad, or a stiff deck brush in corners and edges. The finish should turn to a milky slurry.
  6. Pick up the slurry with a wet vacuum or extractor straight away, before it dries back onto the floor.
  7. Neutralise and rinse with a neutral or mild acid rinse, pick it up, then repeat with clean water until the floor squeaks clean and a pH test reads neutral.
  8. Dry fully. The floor must be bone dry before sealer goes down. Trapped moisture clouds the finish and wrecks adhesion. Airmovers help.
  9. Apply sealer in thin, even coats, edges first and then a figure-eight fill. Let each coat cure to the label, typically 2 to 5 coats. Burnish at high speed once cured if you want more gloss.

The neutral rinse is the whole job

Nine times out of ten a strip and seal that fails, with a finish that powders, peels or never gains gloss, failed at step 7 and not step 9. That is CARSI professional judgement from the trainer's experience. Stripper residue is alkaline, and fresh acrylic finish needs a neutral floor to bond. Leave a fifth of the stripper behind and the customer gets a lovely floor for a fortnight and then a chalky, streaky one. Two checks separate a job that lasts a year from a callback in three weeks: the rinse water running clear, and a pH strip that reads neutral.

lessons.title: Safety, the asbestos stop rule and pricing
lessons.contentBody:
Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you can:

  • State the protective equipment and site controls for strip and seal.
  • Apply the asbestos stop rule to an old resilient floor.
  • Price coat count and drying time honestly.

Safety for strip and seal

  • Protective equipment: chemical-grade nitrile gloves, safety glasses or goggles, non-slip closed footwear, and a P2 respirator if the product or the ventilation calls for it. Strippers blister skin and sting eyes.
  • Slip: a stripped or freshly sealed floor is extremely slippery. Keep signs and a cordon up until it is fully cured and safe to walk on.
  • Electrical: RCD-protected leads only. Keep leads and machine bodies out of the slurry. Power at 230 V plus water is an electrocution risk, and the safety switch is what manages it.
  • SDS on site for the stripper, the neutraliser and the sealer, and labels on decanted containers.
  • Ventilation for solvent-boosted strippers.

Old tile can contain asbestos

Vinyl-asbestos tile was widely laid in Australian schools and halls, and in shops before the late 1980s. Aggressive stripping and machine sanding of unknown old tile can release fibres. If a tiled resilient floor looks like it was laid before 1990 and you do not know its history, stop, do not disturb it, and refer it for assessment. Safe Work Australia's asbestos rules govern here, not the finish maker. In New Zealand, check the current asbestos requirements with WorkSafe New Zealand.

Pricing

Strip and seal is priced per square metre and takes plenty of labour and coats. Two traps:

  • Coat count. A four-coat finish is roughly double the finishing labour of two coats. Quote the coat count.
  • Rinse and dry time. The neutral rinse and the full dry look unbillable and they are not optional. Price them in or you pay for them out of your margin. This is the drying trade-off from Module 4, applied to hard floors.

Take-aways by experience level

  • Newby: Strip and seal is a resilient-floor service, mainly VCT and vinyl. Never strip timber, laminate or stone. Signs and protective equipment from the first drop. Old unknown tile means stop and refer.
  • Intermediate: Run the nine steps and never skip the neutral rinse. Confirm bone dry before sealer, lay thin even coats and quote the coat count.
  • Pro: Tell LVT from VCT and finished from unfinished floors on sight. Trace adhesion failures back to the rinse step, price coat count and cure time honestly, and spot asbestos-risk floors before machinery touches them.

lessons.title: The add-on principle and the one-visit maths
lessons.contentBody:
Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you can:

  • Explain why a second service on the same visit earns a higher margin.
  • Tell an honest add-on offer from a prohibited pressure upsell.

Module 10 taught the six cost lines and three pricing models. This module answers the question that decides whether a run of jobs is profitable or just busy: what else can you honestly sell on the visit you are already standing in?

Inspection-led, not pressure-led

A CARSI add-on is offered because the inspection found a genuine need or opportunity. You disclose it plainly and leave the choice with the customer. "Your traffic lanes will re-soil fast without protector. Here is what it does and what it costs, and it is your call" is a service. Invented urgency and phantom problems are not. They are prohibited under the Australian Consumer Law, which bans misleading conduct. Sell the truth. On a trusted visit the truth sells well enough.

Why add-ons multiply margin

The first service on a visit pays the fixed costs: drive time, set-up, pack-down and the minimum call-out. A second service added while you are already on site skips almost all of that. Your average job value rises much faster than your cost per visit, which makes it the most reliable lever a small operator has on take-home profit. Track average services per visit as a measure alongside your callback rate.

End-of-lease is a standing job type

Roughly a third of Australian households rent. The 2021 Census puts it at about 30.6 per cent (Australian Bureau of Statistics). That makes bond cleaning a steady, repeatable job with good documentation, often with a receipt the tenant needs to get their bond back. It rewards a clean, dated, photographed report, and your drying discipline from Module 4 and the pre-inspection sheet become the deliverable.

lessons.title: Vehicles, boats or caravans: remove the fuel hazard first
lessons.contentBody:
Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you can:

  • List the controls you apply before wet extraction inside an enclosed vehicle, boat or caravan.
  • Explain why petrol vapour is the hazard that matters.

Interior detailing is a natural add-on, but working inside an enclosed vehicle, boat or caravan carries a hazard a carpet-only job does not: petrol vapour. Before any wet extraction or mains-powered cleaning in a closed cabin or cargo space, do these things.

  • Remove any fuel cell, auxiliary tank, jerry can or portable fuel container from the cabin, boot or cargo bay before you start. This is the step skipped most often and it matters most.
  • Ventilate fully. Open every door and hatch and air the space before and during the work. A closed cabin concentrates both fuel vapour and cleaning-solvent fumes.
  • Control ignition. No smoking and no naked flame. Use RCD-protected leads and keep switching gear out of any low-lying vapour.
  • Flag LPG and dual-fuel vehicles, and electric and hybrid ones. LPG systems and high-voltage battery systems have their own isolation requirements. If you are not competent to make them safe, do not proceed.
  • Never run a combustion engine (a truck-mount included) in an unventilated garage or enclosed space. That is a carbon monoxide hazard on top of the fuel-vapour one.

Why vapour sinks to where you work

Petrol vapour is roughly three to four times the density of air. It does not drift up and away. It falls and pools in the lowest enclosed space it finds, which in a car is the footwell and the boot well you are about to soak and extract with a 230 V machine. Your extractor and its leads, plus the switches and the vacuum motor, are all ignition sources. Removing the fuel cell takes the fuel out of the fire triangle, so even if a switch arcs there is nothing at floor level to burn. Make it step one of every vehicle job, written on the pre-inspection sheet, before a hose comes off the van.

lessons.title: Further training, the honest script and what to track
lessons.contentBody:
Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you can:

  • Match add-ons to the kind of further training that backs them.
  • Present an add-on using the four-step honest script.

Add-ons and further training

Some add-ons are backed by further training that you take through schools and examinations approved by the IICRC, for example odour control, rug cleaning, upholstery cleaning, fabric cleaning, commercial carpet maintenance or colour repair. CARSI is accredited as an IICRC CEC provider. They do not replace the school and the exam. A technician trained in carpet cleaning, upholstery work and odour control can offer all three on one visit and charge for each.

Add-onBacked by
DeodorisingOdour-control training
Upholstery and mattress cleaningUpholstery and fabric cleaning training
Rug cleaningRug cleaning training
Commercial maintenance plansCommercial carpet maintenance training
Colour and bleach-spot repairColour repair training
Strip and seal; tile and groutHard-floor competence from Modules 8 and 13

The honest script

  1. Find it at the inspection, not halfway through the clean. Write it on the pre-inspection sheet.
  2. Show the customer the actual condition: the traffic lane, the stained grout, the pet spot.
  3. State plainly what the service does, what it costs, and what happens if they decline. No urgency theatre.
  4. Leave the choice with them and record accept or decline on the job sheet.

Example wording: "While I had the machine out I noticed the grout in your entry is holding soil the mop cannot reach. I can high-pressure clean and seal it today for [price], or leave it. It is entirely your call." It is specific, it is priced and it is optional. That is the whole technique.

What to track

Average services per visit, alongside callback rate. If the first goes up and the second does not, your add-on habit is working.

Take-aways by experience level

  • Newby: Learn the menu and offer only what you can do well. Find add-ons at inspection and disclose them honestly. Never invent a problem. On any vehicle, boat or caravan job, remove enclosed fuel cells and ventilate before you start.
  • Intermediate: Track services per visit and average job value. Attach protector and deodorising to most jobs and quote each service as its own line.
  • Pro: Build packages that combine services, design commercial maintenance cadences, and own repeatable Australian job types such as bond cleans and commercial plans.

lessons.title: Module 14 Knowledge Check: Add-On Services
What the 2026 data says, with its limits
lessons.contentBody:
Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you can:

  • State each finding and where its figure comes from.
  • Explain why a US study is read as directional for an Australian business.

Technical excellence with an empty diary is a hobby. Module 10 protects your margin on each job. This module fills the diary those jobs come from. It rests on one idea the trade under-uses: for a local service business, video connected across your channels is now the front door.

Every figure below carries its source and its limits, so you can weigh it for yourself. Anything without a source is labelled as CARSI professional judgement.

  • The Local Pack is where local customers land. A 2026 WebFX study of 100 US home-services search terms (500 searches) found the Google Local Pack, the top-three map block, in 98 per cent of the searches. It is the one placement you earn through your Google Business Profile, with reviews and relevance, and not one you buy. Read it as directional for an Australian carpet cleaner. It is a US study of home services in general, including heating, plumbing or roofing, and it is not about carpet. The lesson about owning your Local Pack still carries across. This one is verified against the published method.
  • Video is under-used. Publisher-reported figures say videos on Google Business Profiles are viewed about twice as often as photos, while only about 4 per cent of profiles use video (SOCi and Publer). These are publisher-reported and not independently audited, so treat them as a direction and not as proof.
  • Customer photos help. SOCi reports that profiles with customer photos get 42 per cent more direction requests. That is attributed to the publisher and also directional.

The takeaway stands on its own. A complete profile with photos and video engages more people than a bare one.

What was cut, and why

Two popular statistics were left out. One says 76 per cent of local searchers visit within 24 hours. It traces back to a 2016 US retail diary study, which is a decade old, the wrong market and the wrong kind of business. The other says 46 per cent of searches have local intent, and no current primary source could be confirmed. Repeating stale or out-of-context statistics as current fact is a hard stop for CARSI.

lessons.title: The connected system and how to wire it
lessons.contentBody:
Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you can:

  • Name the four accounts in the connected system.
  • Link the accounts so one filming session feeds every channel.

Think of a hub and spokes. YouTube is the library, your Google Business Profile is the shopfront, the social feeds are the reminders and your website closes the sale. One 30-second video, filmed on the job, goes to YouTube, the Google Business Profile, your Facebook Page, Instagram Reels and the matching service page on your website. Connect them once and each new video feeds all of them.

The wiring

  1. Claim or create four accounts under one business identity: a YouTube channel, a Google Business Profile, a Facebook Page and an Instagram Business account.
  2. Link Instagram to the Facebook Page through a Meta Business account so a post or Reel publishes to both. The most common gap is that the two are not linked, which doubles the work.
  3. Add video to the Google Business Profile, not just photos. This is the move almost no one makes.
  4. Put your YouTube link on the website, the Facebook Page, the Instagram bio and the Business Profile.
  5. Link every video description and post back to the matching service page on your site, with the phone number. A tile and grout clip links to the tile and grout page, not the homepage.

lessons.title: What to film, how to measure and the compliance line
lessons.contentBody:
Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you can:

  • Film the five clip types in the recommended format.
  • Measure results over a sensible window.
  • Apply the Australian Consumer Law to before and after images and reviews.

What to film

Home-service customers tend to trust job-site footage over studio ads. You do not need a studio. You need a weekly rhythm, and one useful video a week is enough for most local brands. These points come from practitioner guidance, not from a controlled study. Film the five clips as you work:

ClipWhat to showWhat it does
Before and afterThe traffic lane or stain, then the resultProof, the trade's strongest asset
"Did you know" tipOne 20-second fact, such as blot, do not rubAuthority and repeat views
Service in actionA safe part of the process, such as a wand passShows expertise
Verification clipThe van, uniform, tools, a street sign and one live actionLocal proof for the Business Profile
Result walkthroughThe finished room, shown honestlySupports the sale

The format that holds attention: about 3 seconds of location, then 15 to 20 seconds of the work, then a few seconds of the result. Keep it under 30 seconds, hold the phone steady and skip the long intro.

The image plan

  • A hero before-and-after still for the website service page and the Business Profile photo set.
  • The 30-second video for YouTube, the Business Profile, Facebook, plus an Instagram Reel.
  • Three to five Business Profile photos for each category: exterior, interior, team, equipment, results.
  • A branded thumbnail in your business colours.

Shoot in Australian homes and workplaces, with customer permission on file and no private details in frame. Looking local is the point of local discovery.

Measurement

  • Add UTM tags to the website link on your Business Profile and social bios so the traffic shows up in your analytics.
  • Track the actions that pay: profile calls, website clicks, direction requests and form fills, then lead quality after each upload.
  • Judge over 60 to 90 days, not one week. Video builds familiarity over time.
  • Reviews add up. SOCi reports about a 3 per cent lift in Business Profile conversions for every 10 new reviews. It is an attributed figure, so use it as a direction. Ask for a review after each job as part of the same weekly rhythm.

Market honestly

Everything you publish falls under the Australian Consumer Law. Claims must be truthful and substantiated, testimonials genuine, and before and after images must come from the same real job, never a stock image or a swapped "after". Any incentive or connection behind a review must be disclosed. Sell the truth.

Take-aways by experience level

  • Newby: Claim the four accounts, link Instagram to Facebook, add video to your Google Business Profile, and film one honest before and after this week.
  • Intermediate: Run the weekly one-video rhythm across every channel from one filming session, link each video to its service page, and ask for a review after every job.
  • Pro: Read the analytics over 60 to 90 days, build a content calendar by service and season, and make "the most real, most consistently" your advantage.

lessons.title: Your manual, your certificate and what comes next
lessons.contentBody:
Learning objectives

By the end of this lesson you can:

  • Find and keep your digital copy of the participant manual.
  • Say what you need for the certificate of attendance.
  • Choose a next step with CARSI.

The participant manual

The Participant Take-Home Manual is a CARSI document that follows the two days module by module. It has a quick-reference panel and a take-away for each experience level in every module, plus appendices: a fibre identification field card, pH ranges and safe defaults, the spot removal decision tree, the pre-inspection checklist, and the machinery checklist (daily, then weekly, then monthly). Download it any time from carsi.com.au/workshops/carpet-cleaning: sign in with the email you checked in with and choose Participant manual. It opens as a printable page you can save as a PDF. Printed items are handed out at the close. If you have not received your copy within a few days, contact CARSI through carsi.com.au and say which session you attended. Keep a copy on your phone, and print the field cards for the van.

The certificate of attendance

  • You receive a CARSI certificate of attendance when you have been checked in on both days: once on Day 1 and once on Day 2.
  • If you were checked in on one day only, you do not qualify for the certificate. Talk to your trainer before you leave if your check-in was missed.
  • The certificate records attendance. It is not an IICRC certification and it does not carry IICRC CECs.

Next steps with CARSI

  • Work through Modules 12 to 15 of this course at your own pace. They cover advanced stain removal, then strip and seal, then add-on services and marketing.
  • Look at the other CARSI courses at carsi.com.au. CARSI is accredited as an IICRC CEC provider. IICRC certification itself comes only through schools and examinations approved by the IICRC.
  • Use the pre-inspection form from Module 4 on your next ten jobs and keep a maintenance log from Module 9. Both are free habits that you can start the day after the workshop.

You have spent two days on the van floor. Keep the standards alive in your work.
